title: The Avalanche Auditor
story: At the top of the Snowline Pass stands Vollenbrisk, a frost-coated weigh-master who swears that any caravan whose sleds average more than 90 pounds will shake the ridge loose. Six sleds of ember-coal wait in the wind, and the sixth is still empty. Mr 6 scrapes the frost off the tally board to read the first five weights: 84, 97, 88, 91 and 86 pounds.
question: What must the sixth sled weigh so that the six sleds average exactly 90 pounds?
solution: Six sleds averaging 90 need a total of 6 × 90 = 540 pounds.
The five loaded sleds weigh 84 + 97 + 88 + 91 + 86 = 446 pounds.
So the last sled must hold 540 − 446 = 94 pounds.
praise: Thinking about the average was exactly right — the missing move was turning that average into the total the six sleds need together.
hint: An average of 90 across six sleds tells you the total weight allowed; compare it to what the five sleds already carry.
victory: Mr 6 shovels in precisely 94 pounds, the needle settles dead on 90, and Vollenbrisk sighs, stamps the pass, and lets the caravan tiptoe over the quiet snow.
imagePrompt: A frost-armored auditor creature beside a giant snow-crusted weighing scale on a windy glacier pass, a small numeral 6 knight shovelling ember-coal into the last sled under pale blue dawn light.
